entities.summary: Hans Burgkmair the Elder (1473–1531) was a German painter and woodcut printmaker who played a crucial role in the development of Nuremberg's Renaissance culture. His most famous work, the 'Pfarrer' series, showcased his mastery of woodcuts and his ability to depict the everyday lives of ordinary people. Burgkmair's artistic influence extended beyond his own work, as he helped to establish Nuremberg as a hub for artistic innovation and collaboration. His work also reflects the cultural and religious tensions of the time, as he depicted scenes from the Bible and the lives of the city's Catholic and Protestant populations. Burgkmair's legacy can be seen in the many artists who followed in his footsteps, including his son, Hans Burgkmair the Younger, who continued to work in woodcuts and printmaking. The artist's work also influenced the development of the Mannerist style, which emphasized complex forms and intricate details. Burgkmair's contributions to the world of art and culture are a testament to his skill and innovation, and his work remains an important part of Germany's cultural heritage.
